question: Which of the following is an example of Phylum – Annelida?
solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An example of the **phylum Annelida** is the **earthworm**.
 
• **Earthworms** belong to the class** Clitellata** within the **phylum Annelida.**
 
• They are segmented worms characterized by their long, **cylindrical bodies** divided into **numerous repeated segments**.
 
• **Earthworms **are commonly found in soil and play a vital role in the ecosystem by enhancing soil fertility through their burrowing and decomposition activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Hookworms** are** parasitic worms** that infect the s**mall intestine of humans and other animals.**

 
 
• There are two main species of hookworm that commonly infect humans: **Ancylostoma duodenale and Necator americanus.**
 
• These worms are named for their hook-like mouthparts, which they use to attach to the intestinal lining and feed on blood.
 
• **Hookworm infection** occurs when a person comes into contact with contaminated soil or feces that contain hookworm larvae.
 
• The larvae can penetrate **the skin, usually through bare feet, and migrate through the bloodstream to reach the lungs.**
 
• From there, they are coughed up and swallowed, eventually reaching the small intestine where they mature into adult worms. Adult hookworms then attach to the intestinal wall and start feeding on blood, which can lead to iron deficiency anemia.
 
 
 
• **Filaria worms, also known as filarial nematodes, are a group of parasitic worms that belong to the family Filariidae.**
 
 
• These worms are responsible for causing a group of diseases known as **filariasis or lymphatic filariasis.**
 
• **Filariasis** is a tropical and subtropical disease that affects millions of people worldwide, particularly in regions such as Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific Islands.
 
 
 
• **Roundworms, also known as nematodes, are a diverse group of worms that belong to the phylum Nematoda.**
 
• They are among the most common animals on Earth and can be found in a wide range of** environments, including soil, freshwater, and marine habitats**.
 
• Some roundworms are free-living, while others are parasitic and can infect **plants, animals, and humans.**
